Sam (Sales): Heads-up — Axon wants a short POC tomorrow to validate interactive perf for their web client. Goal: 150 steady qps, plus short microbursts to 1k qps for ~30s every 10m. They care about p99 tail for streaming token delivery (thin client) and cost. Can engineering propose a run plan and a rough cost delta for burst vs baseline?
Devon (SE): Model + max tokens? streaming or non-streaming? Also will they use function calls or plain text gen?
Sam (Sales): Using our curated-7B-ish variant, avg response ~120 tokens, streaming enabled (token-by-token). No function calls.
Maria (Perf): OK. Short summary: baseline 150 qps streaming, bursts 1k qps (30s every 10m). For token-by-token streaming p99 tail is dominated by batching window + network. Two approaches: 1) aggressive micro-batching (batch windows 5–10ms) on Dedicated, 2) conservative single-request path on Hosted with autoscale. I can write a runbook.
Devon (SE): If we test on Dedicated, we can surface steady-state cost and a burst SKU. On Hosted, we need to simulate the burst pattern to validate autoscale latency. Which environment do they want?
Sam (Sales): They want hosted first (fast onboarding) but ask about Dedicated as an option if tail can't meet SLA.
Jon (Infra): For hosted: we'll need quota bump for 1k qps bursts during the window. Also multi-az for safety. If we run a loadlab test from our prod-like cluster, we should tag it to avoid autoscale noise.
Lara (SRE): Add alerts for p95/p99 and queue depth. Recommend a fallback policy: if p99 > 400ms for >30s, route to a cheaper lower-qps model variant. We'll need canary traffic first.
Maria (Perf): Draft runbook snippet below for the loadgen (k6 + our streaming harness). Run locally in k8s loadlab, 10 load generators, use Poisson arrival with bursts.
Maria (Perf): ```
# k6 pseudo config
vus: 120
stages:
  - duration: 10m
    target: 150
# burst every 10m
scheduler: poisson
burst_script: |
  for i in range(30s):
    ramp to 1000 qps
# client uses streaming WS, measure token latencies
```
Devon (SE): Nice. For telemetry: we need token delivery histogram, batch size distribution, and client-side end-to-end p99. Can you instrument the streaming harness to emit per-token timestamps?
Maria (Perf): Yep, we'll emit per-token deltas and rollup p50/p95/p99. Also record KV cache hit rate and batch sizes.
Sam (Sales): Cost ask from customer: what's the delta for 150 qps steady vs adding that burst profile? Give a $/hr ballpark for hosted and a monthly ballpark for Dedicated reserve.
Jon (Infra): Rough hosted delta: baseline 150 qps with that model ~ $X/hr (compute + infra). Adding the burst pattern increases token units due to overhead; estimate extra 20–30% during burst windows. For Dedicated: capacity planning suggests 2x baseline GPUs for burst headroom with short autoscale — monthly commit depends on region, but approx $Y/month for reserved nodes. (I'll follow up with exact numbers after sizing).
Sam (Sales): Can you give a quick min-max: hosted per-hour and Dedicated monthly? I need to share with Axon by EOD.
Maria (Perf): Quick ballpark (very rough): Hosted: $12–25/hr depending on tokens and region, bursts add +$3–8/hr avg across the run. Dedicated: $12k–18k/month for reserved capacity that covers steady+burst headroom; you can do smaller commit + burst credits for lower up-front. I'll convert to a slide.
Sam (Sales): Great. Also they asked about security — will the streaming socket touch customer data? They want encryption + retention policy.
Jon (Infra): Hosted streaming uses TLS end-to-end. We can disable logging of payloads and enforce short retention on request bodies. For Dedicated/Private we provide customer-managed VPC and KMS.
Lara (SRE): Put this in an FAQ: if streaming performance degrades, we fail open to a smaller model; ensure fallbacks are audited.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: loadlab/streaming-harness v2.4 to cluster-loadlab (id: deploy-8421) :rocket:
Devon (SE): I'll coordinate the test window with Axon and send them the exact curl/ws harness and the execution playbook. Sam, want me to run a smoke tonight?
Sam (Sales): Yes please — smoke tonight at low QPS and full run tomorrow 10:00 PT. Share results in this thread. :thumbsup: :eyes:
Maria (Perf): I'll run baseline smoke + one burst run and post a short writeup with p50/p95/p99, batch histograms, and a cost estimate. Expect initial artifacts in ~3 hours after smoke.
Sam (Sales): Thanks all — I'll prep the customer note and include the run times.
